co_upper_security_risk.blurb: A steep, mostly bolted cliff on the high north side of Boulder Canyon, above the road and a stiff uphill walk from the canyon floor. Seventeen routes split between ten sport lines and seven trad lines, with the grades fairly evenly spread from 5.9 up to 5.13. Many lines are long single pitches, so carry plenty of quickdraws, and the crack lines are hard on the hands. The wall faces south, which makes it a popular cold-weather choice, though it can feel breezy. It sits beside Lower and Higher Security Risk, so you can link several walls in one day.

co_sharksfin.blurb: A fin-shaped formation in The Crags, on the hillside above Estes Park, with a subalpine, almost mountaineering atmosphere. Most of its seventeen routes are trad, with four bolted lines, and grades run from easy fifth class to about 5.11, with 5.8 to 5.10 the bulk of it. Lines go from a single pitch to three pitches on every side, so it suits a short multi-pitch day. Descents are by rappel or a fifth-class scramble. The southwest side picks up afternoon sun and is cooler early, while the north side stays shaded. Views to the west make storms easy to watch building.

co_west_face_6.blurb: The west-facing side of North Gateway Rock in Garden of the Gods, Colorado Springs, and the wall holding most of the rock's lines. It catches afternoon sun. Seventeen routes mix nine trad, six sport and two aid lines, with grades from the mid 5.5s to the low 5.12s and the heaviest cluster at 5.11 and 5.12. A few routes are multi-pitch. Reaching the base means walking in from the north main lot and then taking a low-angle sandy ramp with some third-class steps. The park bans white chalk, so bring a colour that blends with the stone.

co_wasp_canyon_the.blurb: A canyon-shaped section of Thunder Ridge in the South Platte area, reached by a cairned path over ledges and a talus slope. Of seventeen climbs, twelve are trad, three sport and two boulder problems, ranging from 5.7 to about 5.13 with a lot of 5.12. It is known for steep, overhanging stone, including a roofed wall about forty feet high. Much of the ridge faces south, but this canyon stays shadier, which makes it a good summer pick when other walls are baking. Thunder Ridge is quiet, so you will probably have the place largely to yourself.

co_c_section.blurb: A south-facing sport wall in Castlewood Canyon State Park, southeast of Denver, also known as the Hedgeclipper area. Sixteen routes, fourteen of them sport, with one top-rope and one trad line. Most sit around 5.11, with a handful of easier lines in the 5.7 to 5.10 range and a couple at 5.12. Routes are moderate in height. Because it faces south it warms up well, a good fit for cold days. Walk in from the farthest south lot on the creekside path, passing a waterfall, crossing the creek and doubling back north to the base.

co_wall_of_justice.blurb: A steep, overhanging sport wall in Clear Creek Canyon near Golden, in the Tunnel 2 East sector. It was once a crumbling overhang but has been cleaned up into a sought-after destination for harder climbing. Of sixteen routes, fifteen are bolted and one is a top-rope. Grades start around 5.8 but the weight sits in the 5.11 to 5.12 range, with a couple of lines climbing into the 5.13 and 5.14 range. Expect short, powerful, sustained routes rather than long pitches, with a roof section as the centerpiece of the wall.

co_transmitter_tower.blurb: A tucked-away sport crag outside Buena Vista, a short stroll beyond Split Rock, with a high, open setting and views toward the Collegiate Peaks. Sixteen routes, fourteen of them bolted single pitches, plus one top-rope and one trad line, on textured stone with pockets and small edges. Grades run from the 5.6 range to 5.11, with most lines at 5.9 and 5.10, which suits climbers stepping up from easier sport. The crag is easy to miss from a distance, so look for the obvious pile of rock past the hill. Mountain weather can turn quickly, with wind and cooler temperatures even when the valley is warm.

_expect.name: West Ridge - part F - The Potato Chip

co_west_ridge_part_f_the_potato_chip.blurb: A large flake of rock jutting west from the upper West Ridge of Eldorado Canyon, below Shirttail Peak. It is remote and rarely visited, reached by a long, steep hike on the Rincon Trail and then a gully. Sixteen routes, fourteen trad and two sport, from the 5.6 range up to 5.13 with most lines between 5.8 and 5.10. A bolted line runs up the south side and a trad line up the west side. The ridge is exposed and sunny, and the summit can be reached by scrambling along the ridge crest. Expect solitude, long views and a committing day.
